as_told.title: Lue Elizondo's book: warp bubble discussed with Hal Puthoff

plain: A book by Lue Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who ran a small office that studied unexplained aerial reports, is said to explain why UFOs come in the shapes they do: they would carry some kind of anti-gravity device. A US congressman named Eric Burlison says the book describes it this way, so that the shapes "seem to make sense" once you picture a device that cancels gravity around the craft. A former scientist with DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, named John Blitch, also points to the book. He says it shows a "warp bubble", a pocket of bent space around a craft, which Elizondo had discussed with a physicist named Hal Puthoff. Both men are summarising the book from their own reading, not from anything they saw. The idea matters because it would offer a physical reason for the odd forms witnesses report.
